drivingQuestion: How and when must a person complete the weekly Torah portion together with the congregation?
outcomeNote: The timing of the portions is settled — neither early nor late — and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's synagogue ruling is upheld with Abaye's three qualifications.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: לְעוֹלָם יַשְׁלִים אָדָם פָּרָשִׁיּוֹתָיו עִם הַצִּבּוּר. שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם.
segments.en: «Rav Huna bar Yehuda said» that «Rabbi Ami said: A person should always complete his» Torah «portions with the congregation.» The congregation reads a particular Torah portion every Shabbat, and during the week prior to each Shabbat, one is required to read the «Bible» text of the weekly portion «twice and» the «translation once.»

segments.he: וַאֲפִילּוּ ״עֲטָרוֹת וְדִיבֹן״. שֶׁכָּל הַמַּשְׁלִים פָּרָשִׁיּוֹתָיו עִם הַצִּבּוּר מֵאֲרִיכִין לוֹ יָמָיו וּשְׁנוֹתָיו.
segments.en: This applies to every verse, «even» a verse like: «“Atarot and Divon» and Yazer and Nimra and Ḥeshbon and Elaleh and Sevam and Nevo and Beon” (Numbers 32:3). While that verse is comprised entirely of names of places that are identical in Hebrew and Aramaic, one is nevertheless required to read the verse twice and its translation once, «as one who completes his» Torah «portions with the congregation» is rewarded that «his days and years are extended.»

segments.he: רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי סָבַר לְאַשְׁלוֹמִינְהוּ לְפָרָשְׁיָיתָא דְּכֹלָּא שַׁתָּא בְּמַעֲלֵי יוֹמָא דְכִפּוּרֵי, תְּנָא לֵיהּ חִיָּיא בַּר רַב מִדִּפְתִּי: כְּתִיב: ״וְעִנִּיתֶם אֶת נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם בְּתִשְׁעָה לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּעֶרֶב״.
segments.en: «Rav Beivai bar Abaye thought to finish all the» Torah «portions of the entire year,» which he had been unable to complete at their appointed time, «on the eve of Yom Kippur» when he would have time to do so. But «Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti taught him: It is written» with regard to Yom Kippur: «“And you shall afflict your souls on the ninth day of the month in the evening,» from evening to evening you shall keep your Sabbath” (Leviticus 23:32).

segments.he: וְכִי בְּתִשְׁעָה מִתְעַנִּין?! וַהֲלֹא בַּעֲשָׂרָה מִתְעַנִּין! אֶלָּא לוֹמַר לְךָ כָּל הָאוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה בִּתְשִׁיעִי, מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִילּוּ מִתְעַנֶּה תְּשִׁיעִי וַעֲשִׂירִי.
segments.en: The Gemara wonders: «And does one fast on the ninth» of Tishrei? «Doesn’t one fast on the tenth of Tishrei,» as the Torah says at the beginning of that portion: “However, on the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement; there shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall afflict your souls” (Leviticus 23:27)? «Rather,» this verse comes «to tell you: One who eats and drinks on the ninth» day of Tishrei in preparation for the fast the next day, «the verse ascribes him» credit «as if he fasted on» both «the ninth and the tenth» of Tishrei. Ḥiyya bar Rav of Difti cited this verse to Rav Beivai bar Abaye to teach him that Yom Kippur eve is dedicated to eating and drinking, not to completing the Torah portions one may have missed throughout the year.

segments.he: סָבַר לְאַקְדּוֹמִינְהוּ, אָמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא, תְּנֵינָא: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַקְדִּים וְשֶׁלֹּא יְאַחֵר.
segments.en: When Rav Beivai heard this, «he thought to» read the Torah portions «earlier,» before they were to be read by the community. «A certain» unnamed «elder told him, we learned: As long as one does not» read the Torah portions «earlier or later» than the congregation. One must read them together with the congregation.

segments.he: כְּדַאֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְנֵיהּ: אַשְׁלִימוּ פָּרָשְׁיוֹתַיְיכוּ עִם הַצִּבּוּר שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם.
segments.en: «As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi told his sons: Complete your portions with the congregation, the Bible» text «twice and» the «translation once.»

segments.he: וְהִזָּהֲרוּ בִּוְרִידִין כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּשְׁחוֹט אֶת הַוְּרִידִין.
segments.en: He also advised them: «Be careful with the» jugular «veins, in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, as we learned» in a mishna with regard to the laws of ritual slaughter: «Rabbi Yehuda said:» Cutting the trachea and esophagus in the ritual slaughter of a bird does not render the bird kosher «until he slaughters the» jugular «veins» as well. While this is not halakhically required, it is appropriate to do so to prevent significant amounts of blood from remaining in the bird.

segments.he: וְהִזָּהֲרוּ בְּזָקֵן שֶׁשָּׁכַח תַּלְמוּדוֹ מֵחֲמַת אוֹנְסוֹ. דְּאָמְרִינַן: לוּחוֹת וְשִׁבְרֵי לוּחוֹת מוּנָּחוֹת בָּאָרוֹן.
segments.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi further advised: «And be careful» to continue to respect «an elder who has forgotten his» Torah «knowledge due to» circumstances «beyond his control.» Even though he is no longer a Torah scholar, he must still be respected for the Torah that he once possessed. «As we say:» Both «the tablets» of the Covenant «and the broken tablets are placed in the Ark» of the Covenant in the Temple. Even though the first tablets were broken, their sanctity obligates one not to treat them with contempt. An elder who forgot the Torah knowledge he once possessed is likened to these broken tablets.

segments.he: אָמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לִבְנֵיהּ: כְּשֶׁאַתֶּם חוֹתְכִין בָּשָׂר, אַל תַּחְתְּכוּ עַל גַּב הַיָּד. אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: מִשּׁוּם סַכָּנָה. וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: מִשּׁוּם קִלְקוּל סְעוּדָה.
segments.en: «Rava said to his sons» three bits of advice: «When you cut meat, do not cut it on your hand.» The Gemara offers two explanations for this. «Some say: Due to» the «danger» that one might accidentally cut his hand, «and some say: Due to» the fact that it could «ruin the meal,» as even if one only cut himself slightly, that small amount of blood could still spoil the meat and render it repulsive to eat.

segments.he: וְאַל תֵּשְׁבוּ עַל מִטַּת אֲרַמִּית, וְאַל תַּעַבְרוּ אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין. וְאַל תֵּשְׁבוּ עַל מִטַּת אֲרַמִּית, אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי לָא תִּגְנוֹ בְּלָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי דְּלָא תִּנְסְבוּ גִּיּוֹרְתָא. וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, אֲרַמִּית מַמָּשׁ.
segments.en: «And» Rava also advised: «Do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman, and do not pass by a synagogue when the community is praying.» The Gemara explains: «Some say: Do not sit on the bed of an Aramean woman» means «one should not go to sleep without reciting Shema,» as by doing so, it is tantamount to sleeping in the bed of a non-Jew, as his conduct is unbecoming a Jew. «Others say:» This means that «one should not marry a woman who converted,» and it is better to marry a woman who was born Jewish. «And some say:» It «literally» means that one should not sit on the bed of «an Aramean,» i.e., a non-Jewish «woman.»

segments.he: וּמִשּׁוּם מַעֲשֶׂה דְרַב פָּפָּא. דְּרַב פָּפָּא אֲזַל לְגַבֵּי אֲרַמִּית, הוֹצִיאָה לוֹ מִטָּה. אָמְרָה לוֹ: שֵׁב! אָמַר לָהּ: אֵינִי יוֹשֵׁב, עַד שֶׁתַּגְבִּיהִי אֶת הַמִּטָּה. הִגְבִּיהָה אֶת הַמִּטָּה וּמָצְאוּ שָׁם תִּינוֹק מֵת. מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים: אָסוּר לֵישֵׁב עַל מִטַּת אֲרַמִּית.
segments.en: This bit of advice was «due to an incident» involving «Rav Pappa. Rav Pappa went to» visit «an Aramean woman. She took out a bed» and «she said to him: Sit. He said to her: I will not sit until you lift the» sheets covering the «bed.» She did so «and they found a dead baby there.» Had Rav Pappa sat upon the bed, he would have been blamed for killing the baby. «From» that incident, «the Sages said: One is prohibited from sitting on the bed of an Aramean woman.»

segments.he: וְאַל תַּעַבְרוּ אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין — מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: אָסוּר לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲבוֹר אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהַצִּבּוּר מִתְפַּלְּלִין.
segments.en: «And» Rava’s third bit of advice was, «do not pass behind a synagogue while the congregation is praying. This» statement «supports» the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,» as «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One is prohibited from passing behind a synagogue while the congregation is praying» because they will suspect that he does not want to pray, and it is a show of contempt for the synagogue.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲבָל אִיכָּא פִּתְחָא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵית לָן בַּהּ. וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלֵיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא, אֲבָל אִיכָּא בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא אַחֲרִינָא — לֵית לָן בַּהּ. וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא דָּרֵי טוּנָא, וְלָא רָהֵיט, וְלָא מַנַּח תְּפִילִּין, אֲבָל אִיכָּא חַד מֵהָנָךְ — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
segments.en: «Abaye» introduced several caveats to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s statement and «said:» «We only said» this prohibition if «there is no other entrance» to the synagogue, «but» if «there is» another entrance, since it is possible that he will simply use the second entrance, they will not suspect him, and the prohibition «does not apply.» «And we only said» this prohibition if «there is no other synagogue» in the city, «but» if «there is another synagogue,» the prohibition «does not apply.» «And we only said» this prohibition when «he is not carrying a burden, and not running, and not wearing phylacteries. But» if «one of those» factors «applies», the prohibition «does not apply.» If he is carrying a burden or running, clearly he is occupied with his work. If he is wearing phylacteries, it is evident that he is a God-fearing individual and they will not suspect him.

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא בר יהודה, אמר רבי אמי: לעולם ישלים אדם פרשיותיו עם הצבור
moves.summary: One must always complete the weekly portion with the congregation, twice in Scripture and once in translation.
moves.about: the duty to complete the weekly portion twice in Scripture and once in translation

moves.cueHe: ואפילו ״עטרות ודיבן״
moves.summary: The rule covers even a verse of bare place names, and the reward is long life.
moves.about: even a verse of bare place names must be read twice with its translation

moves.cueHe: רב ביבי בר אביי סבר לאשלומינהו לפרשייתא דכולא שתא
moves.summary: Rav Beivai bar Abaye plans to make up the whole year's portions on Yom Kippur eve.
moves.about: his plan to make up the whole year's portions on Yom Kippur eve

moves.cueHe: תנא ליה חייא בר רב מדפתי: כתיב ״ועניתם את נפשתיכם בתשעה לחדש בערב״
moves.summary: He is taught the verse that makes Yom Kippur eve a day for eating and drinking.
moves.about: whether Yom Kippur eve may be spent completing the year's unread portions rather than eating and drinking

moves.cueHe: וכי בתשעה מתענין?! והלא בעשרה מתענין!
moves.summary: The verse cannot mean a fast on the ninth, since the fast is on the tenth.
moves.about: the fast is on the tenth of Tishrei, not the ninth, so the verse cannot mean what it says

moves.cueHe: אלא לומר לך
moves.summary: Eating and drinking on the ninth is credited as if one had fasted both days.
moves.about: how the verse can command affliction on the ninth

moves.cueHe: סבר לאקדומינהו
moves.summary: Rav Beivai then plans to read the portions ahead of the congregation instead.
moves.about: his second plan, to read the portions ahead of the congregation

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה ההוא סבא, תנינא: ובלבד שלא יקדים ושלא יאחר
moves.summary: A certain elder cites the taught rule that one may neither anticipate nor delay.
moves.about: whether the weekly portions may be read ahead of the congregation

moves.cueHe: כדאמר להו רבי יהושע בן לוי לבניה
moves.summary: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's charge to his sons is brought as the same ruling.
moves.about: his charge to his sons to complete the portions with the congregation

moves.cueHe: והזהרו בורידין כרבי יהודה
moves.summary: His second charge: be careful with the jugular veins, following Rabbi Yehuda.
moves.about: his instruction to be careful with the jugular veins in slaughter

moves.cueHe: דתנן: רבי יהודה אומר: עד שישחוט את הורידין
moves.summary: The mishna in which Rabbi Yehuda requires cutting the veins is identified.
moves.about: the mishna in which Rabbi Yehuda requires cutting the veins

moves.cueHe: והזהרו בזקן ששכח תלמודו מחמת אונסו
moves.summary: His third charge: honour an elder who has forgotten his learning through no fault of his own.
moves.about: his instruction to honour an elder who forgot his learning through no fault of his own

moves.cueHe: דאמרינן: לוחות ושברי לוחות מונחות בארון
moves.summary: The broken tablets kept beside the whole ones in the Ark ground that respect.
moves.about: the received dictum that the tablets and the broken tablets alike rest in the Ark

moves.cueHe: אמר להו רבא לבניה: כשאתם חותכין בשר
moves.summary: Rava's parallel counsel to his sons opens: do not cut meat resting on the hand.
moves.about: his instruction not to cut meat resting on the hand

moves.cueHe: איכא דאמרי: משום סכנה
moves.summary: Two reasons are offered for the warning: danger, or spoiling the meal.
moves.about: why Rava forbade cutting meat on the hand — danger, or spoiling the meal

moves.cueHe: ואל תשבו על מטת ארמית, ואל תעברו אחורי בית הכנסת
moves.summary: Rava's two further counsels are stated.
moves.about: his further instructions not to sit on an Aramean woman's bed and not to pass behind a synagogue during prayer

moves.cueHe: ואל תשבו על מטת ארמית, איכא דאמרי לא תגנו בלא קריאת שמע
moves.summary: Three readings of the bed of an Aramean woman are recorded, the last literal.
moves.about: what Rava meant by the bed of an Aramean woman

moves.cueHe: ומשום מעשה דרב פפא
moves.summary: The incident of Rav Pappa, the woman's bed and the dead infant is told.
moves.about: the incident in which he refused to sit until the bed was lifted and a dead infant was found

moves.cueHe: מכאן אמרו חכמים: אסור לישב על מטת ארמית
moves.summary: From that incident the Sages forbade sitting on the bed of a gentile woman.

moves.cueHe: מסייע ליה לרבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: Rava's third counsel is noted as support for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's ruling, which is then quoted.
moves.about: his ruling forbidding passage behind a synagogue during prayer

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: ולא אמרן אלא דליכא פתחא אחרינא
moves.summary: Abaye limits the prohibition with three conditions, all turning on whether suspicion is possible.
moves.about: the prohibition holds only where there is no second entrance, no second synagogue, and the passer-by carries nothing, is not running and wears no phylacteries
